verdict.useCase: An agent that reads a user's Spotify library and playlists and controls playback on their behalf, using the Web API Authorization Code flow

timeToCredentials.basis: Our estimate: registration needs only a developer account and a dashboard form (no source states a time), and typical instant app registration takes minutes to an hour or two.

timeToProduction.basis: Spotify's quota-modes page says the extended-quota review can take up to six weeks, and that it accepts applications only from organizations (not individuals) with at least 250,000 monthly active users. The minimum wait is not stated.

humanEffortHours.basis: Our estimate: creating the app, wiring the Authorization Code flow and refresh handling, choosing scopes and testing playback and library calls. No source gives effort figures.

verdict.summary: Spotify requires you to register your own app; Composio lists no managed Spotify app. Registering takes minutes, but a Development Mode app needs a Premium owner and supports only 5 allowlisted users. Serving more users needs extended quota, which Spotify accepts only from registered organizations with at least 250,000 monthly active users, after a review of up to six weeks.
verdict.biggestLaunchRisk: Extended quota is the hard gate: Spotify accepts applications only from organizations with at least 250,000 monthly active users, and the review can take up to six weeks. Until then you are limited to 5 allowlisted users and a Premium app owner.

inference.rationale: Typically, moving from a development/quota-limited mode to broader access involves a manual provider review of the app and use case. The captured sources do not describe the review process, so this is a cautious guess.

youNeedOwnWhen.text: Always, for Spotify: Composio's managed-auth directory lists Spotify under 'Bring your own OAuth app', so you register your own Spotify app even for prototyping.

scopesAndNuances.text: Development Mode quota is counted per developer account, not per Client ID. All your Development Mode apps share one budget.
A developer account can have up to 25 Client IDs (raised from 1).
When the quota is exceeded, the 429 response body includes "reason": "QUOTA_EXCEEDED". Rate-limit 429s do not carry this reason.
Spotify Open Access is a separate partner API for approved partners only, with Client IDs allow-listed by Partner Management. It does not clearly apply to a standard Web API agent.

The Android auth-lib is a Beta library that returns an authorization code through the Spotify client. It requires an application fingerprint and falls back to a web login if Spotify is not installed. It is only relevant if your agent has an Android client.
The provider's published OAuth metadata lists: 3 scope(s) listed; PKCE: S256; no registration endpoint is listed.

blockers.fix: Reduce call volume and cache library and playlist reads. Keep Development Mode apps to what you need, since they share one quota. Look for an extended-quota route in the dashboard or the docs.

blockers.problem: Other users' accounts cannot use the app: a Development Mode app supports up to 5 authenticated users, each added to the app's allowlist.
blockers.fix: Apply for extended quota, which Spotify accepts only from registered organizations with at least 250,000 monthly active users; review can take up to six weeks. Until then, keep use to the allowlisted users.
